claims.hypothesis: SED-model dust masses differ from optically thin millimeter-flux masses
claims.experiment: Fit ANN-DIAD SED models to 178 disks and recompute flux-based masses with the Hildebrand equation
claims.result: SED-model masses are on average about a factor 2.0 higher
claims.finding: Flux-based masses underestimate disk dust mass because many disks are optically thick at 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: Disk dust masses calculated from SED modeling are, on average, a factor of 2.0 times higher for both Serpens and L1641/L1647 than those computed using mm-fluxes at 1.3mm.

claims.hypothesis: The mass discrepancy is driven by optical depth
claims.experiment: Compute flux-weighted mean optical depth at 1.3 mm and compare with dust mass, disk size and discrepancy factor
claims.result: Mean optical depth rises with dust mass and falls with disk size and correlates with the discrepancy factor
claims.finding: High optical depth at (sub-)mm wavelengths causes the underestimates

evidence.loc: 4.1 The importance of optical depth when deriving disk masses
evidence.quote: flux-based disk dust masses are underestimated to a greater extent for disks that are more massive and/or more compact

claims.hypothesis: Longer wavelengths trace dust mass better
claims.experiment: Compute optical depth at 7 mm (ALMA band 1) for the same disks
claims.result: The vast majority of objects become optically thin at 7 mm
claims.finding: Observations at band 3 and band 1 are essential to measure disk dust masses

evidence.quote: We find that the vast majority of objects become optically thin at 7 mm.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust masses depend on fixed DIAD assumptions (dust composition, gas-to-dust ratio, no substructure), so the factor of 2 may be model-dependent
Fit quality cuts are judged by eye and remove 33 sources, which may bias the result toward well-behaved disks
Flux-based comparison uses a constant 20 K, which may exaggerate the discrepancy for luminous stars
No independent test of the SED masses, such as longer-wavelength fluxes, is shown
